newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says plans export tax on coconut products.
newsitem.headline: Manila says plans export tax on coconut products.

text.p: The Philippines is studying plans to re-impose taxes on the export of raw-material products including copra and coconut oil, officials from the Department of Trade and Industry said.

The proposed export tax on raw materials was aimed at encouraging the export of value-added products and to promote more investment in the setting up of processing plants in the country, Trade undersecretary Melito Salazar said in an interview.
The proposal is also intended to discourage exports in favour of selling to the domestic market.
"The proposed export tax is still in its early stage. It is just one of the schemes we are looking at to promote value-added exports," Salazar said.
The high export tax on copra during the rule of former President Ferdinand Marcos spawned the development of more coconut oil mills in the '70s, Salazar said.
At that time, copra exports were slapped a 10 percent tax and coconut oil exports were taxed at three percent.
The export tax on coconut products were removed after President Corazon Aquino assumed power in 1986, industry officials said.
Philippine vegetable oil dealers said the re-imposition of taxes on coconut products would push up prices higher.
"If they (the government) impose a tax on copra it is negligible because we only export very little. But if it is on coconut oil, it's a different story," said one trader.
"Any input on taxes will bring up prices of coconut products," another Manila trader said.
"If the market is bullish, buyers would be willing to absorb the tax cost. But when the market is bearish it would eat up the export proceeds of millers and planters," another trader said.
Coconut oil prices hit a 10-year high in June this year due to tight supplies from the Philippines.

Data from the trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines Inc showed average monthly prices of the country's coconut oil exports hit $830 per tonne FOB in June, the highest price since it fetched $839 per tonne in January 1985.
The coconut crop in the Philippines, the world's largest exporter of coconut oil, is expected to rise by 8.9 percent to 2.141 million tonnes in 1997 from this year's forecast 1.966 million.
